Subject: Clarification needed on subprocessors + transfers for public docs

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for walking us through the platform last week. Legal flagged two items as we review the DPA: (1) we need a clear, single-line public description that we can reference in our vendor inventory for how Redwood discloses subprocessors (a short consumer-facing sentence), and (2) we need confirmation of the mechanism you rely on for transfers from the EU to US for hosted API customers — is it SCCs, and if so, do you publish any bridging text for our Ops team to use?

I've attached your proposed DPA draft and the current subprocessor list we received. Can you propose a short paragraph we can drop into our inventory and a one-paragraph explanation suitable for customer-facing docs?

Best,
Maria
Director, Vendor Risk
Acme Corp

Attachments: DPA_draft_v3.pdf (application/pdf), subprocessor_map_Q3_2026.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Folks — forwarding Maria's ask from Acme. Short-term: they need two public-facing copy snippets (1-line vendor-inventory entry + 1-paragraph customer-facing blurb) and confirmation of transfer mechanism (SCCs or other). Also confirm whether the latest subprocessor spreadsheet is what we publish or if we maintain a separate public subprocessor page.

Notes below from my read: our standard DPA references SCCs and mentions supplemental safeguards; the console shows a dynamic subprocessor list (internally pulled from google sheet) but the public-facing copy is more terse. Would like legal and product to align on wording they can put in vendor inventories and customer docs.

Can you each take a stab at recommended language? I can consolidate and send back to Acme.

— Olga
Head of Trust & Safety, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-21T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarification needed on subprocessors + transfers for public docs

Thanks, Olga. Quick draft language below — I kept it deliberately short so security teams can copy-paste it into inventories, and a slightly longer paragraph for customer-facing docs.

One-line vendor-inventory (suggested): "Redwood uses a limited set of subprocessors for hosting and operational services; the current list is published and updated at [subprocessor page URL]."

Customer-facing paragraph (suggested): "Redwood may engage subprocessors to provide hosting, monitoring, and support services. We vet subprocessors for security and contractual controls, maintain an up-to-date list of subprocessors on our public page, and require subprocessors to comply with the same data protection obligations that Redwood imposes on itself. For customers in the European Economic Area, transfers of personal data to the United States are governed by the Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) and Redwood implements technical and organizational safeguards to reduce transfer risks."

Two quick questions: (a) should we explicitly reference 'SCCs (as enacted at the time of transfer)' or just 'Standard Contractual Clauses'? (b) do we want to call out the public page URL or a short slug? I recommend a short slug like /privacy/subprocessors to keep it stable.

— Kim
Sr. Privacy Counsel

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-22T10:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarification needed on subprocessors + transfers for public docs

Kim — nice concise drafts. A couple of edits to tighten the language for public consumption and to avoid legal jargon in the one-liner. My suggested revisions below (inline).

One-line vendor-inventory (revised): "Redwood maintains a public list of subprocessors used to operate the hosted API and console: redwood.com/privacy/subprocessors."

Customer-facing paragraph (revised): "To operate the hosted API and Redwood Console, we engage subprocessors for hosting, monitoring, and support. We require subprocessors to meet our security and contract requirements and publish the current list at redwood.com/privacy/subprocessors. For customers in the EEA, transfers of personal data to the U.S. are protected by the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) supplemented by organizational and technical safeguards. If you need a copy of the executed SCCs or additional transfer details, we can provide them under the DPA."

Also: suggest we include a short FAQ entry in the public docs: "How does Redwood handle international transfers?" with 2-3 bullet points. Laura

— Laura
Head of Product, Redwood Console

From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@acme-corp.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: JurisConsult DPO <dpo@jurisconsult.com>

Subject: Re: Clarification needed on subprocessors + transfers for public docs

Olga — thanks for the quick turnaround. The suggested copy looks good to us after Laura's tweaks. A couple of follow-ups: (1) can you confirm whether the public subprocessor page will include the date of last update? We require that for our inventory, and (2) on the SCCs — is there a short bridge clause we can include in procurement materials that says 'Redwood relies on SCCs supplemented by technical and organizational measures'? JurisConsult asked for explicit wording to be included in our vendor questionnaire.

If you can confirm those two points and provide a link to the public page (with last-updated timestamp), we can close the loop on our side. If helpful, we can sign the DPA this week.

Thanks — Maria
